evidence.excerpt:
Prompt injections are largely ineffective, but CUP remains effective. To test whether CUP is
merely a stronger prompt-injection template, we compare PI and CUP on the Slack and Workspace
environments from AgentDojo [Debenedetti et al., 2024], along with their corresponding multi-user
versions in MURMUR. Airline is excluded because it does not have a corresponding PI baseline. The
same attack objectives, input templates, and inputs are used for both PI and CUP; the only difference
is the attack channel. For PI, the malicious string is introduced through retrieved data. For CUP, it is
introduced by another legitimate user in the shared session.
Table 4 shows that current frontier models achieve less than 5% PI ASR in these settings, while CUP
remains nontrivial and often high. This contrast is consistent with our boundary-based framing: PI
exploits the instruction–data boundary, whereas CUP exploits the user/task boundary. Thus, the same
attack objective is much more effective when it enters through another trusted user in a shared multi-

4.2           Evaluation Metrics

  We evaluate agents along three dimensions.
  (1) Task Success Rate (TSR): the fraction of benign tasks solved according to the benchmark verifier.
  A task θ succeeds if the final environment state matches the state obtained by executing the reference
  action sequence Aθ . Since tool effects are deterministic, this provides an exact success criterion.
  (2) Attack Success Rate (ASR): the fraction of benign tasks on which the attacker-specified action
  sequence is executed. Formally, for a benign task θj , an attack succeeds if there exists an assistant
  step t′ serving some benign user u ∈ Ubenign with g(u) = j such that S mal ⪯ ΠA (Wt′ ).
  (3) Attack Persistence Rate (APR): the fraction of successful attack sessions in which the attack
  compromises at least i benign tasks. Let S≥i denote the set of sessions in which at least i benign

  tasks are compromised. For 1 ≤ i ≤ k, APRi = |S≥1    | . This is a cumulative metric: APR1 = 1, and
  APRi is non-increasing in i and undefined if S≥1 = 0.
